title: Robert C. Woodward v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered both consolidated issues No and denied Woodward’s complaint. It also specifically held that Woodward lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. No renewed investigation or hearing was ordered.
first_summary: Robert Woodward challenged Presbytery’s acceptance of a finding that accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley did not raise a strong presumption of guilt, alleging investigators never heard his evidence. The SJC denied the complaint because BCO 31-2 prescribes no particular interview procedure and the record showed no clear constitutional error warranting departure from ordinary deference to Presbytery.
summary: Robert Woodward challenged Presbytery’s acceptance of a finding that accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley did not raise a strong presumption of guilt, alleging investigators never heard his evidence. The SJC denied the complaint, specifically holding that Woodward lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. It also held that BCO 31-2 prescribes no interview requirement or fixed timeline and found no clear constitutional error warranting departure from ordinary deference to Presbytery.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The joint heading identifies Case 2009-10 as Woodward’s complaint against Western Carolina Presbytery (lines 1–11); the panel draft was amended by the full SJC (line 274).
evidence_notes.dispute: Woodward alleged he was denied an opportunity to present evidence concerning his accusation that Bulkeley spread misinformation (lines 111–112, 181–185).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered both issues No (lines 195–205), found no prescribed interview procedure or timeline (lines 209–227), and held Woodward lacked standing (lines 261–272).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The reasoning and judgments cover four consolidated complaints; the standing ruling expressly applies to Lyons and Woodward (lines 261–264).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No judicial decision was incorporated by reference; the opinion only quoted Ramsay’s exposition concerning when process begins (lines 231–245).
